subtype: Approach: buys something on a sudden urge [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Yogesh, and I still feel a little sick thinking about last Diwali. Relatives had given me festival money, and I had promised myself to keep some for school books and notebooks in June. Then an advertisement popped up: a tiny speaker with coloured lights, today only. My heart raced. I did not ask anyone, not even Lalit, who was with me at the shop. I bought it in ten minutes. It sounded fine for a week. When June came, the book fee and the notebooks were due and my pocket was empty. I had to ask Papa, who was tired after work and did not say much. That silence was worse than a scolding.

qa.a: Yogesh bought a tiny speaker with coloured lights.

qa.q: How did Yogesh feel when June came and the pocket was empty?
qa.a: Yogesh felt ashamed and regretful, and Papa's silence made it worse.

qa.q: What could Yogesh do next time an advertisement tempts Yogesh?
qa.a: Yogesh could wait a day and check the school needs first, or ask a trusted person before buying.

qa.q: How might Papa have felt when asked for the money?
qa.a: Papa may have felt tired, disappointed or worried, and chose silence over words.

grounding: Shows a teenager spending festival money on an advertised gadget on impulse and later lacking money for books and notebooks.

subtype: Approach: buys something on a sudden urge [Pitfall]
passage:
Class teacher's note: Dhruv, Class 9, after the Diwali break

Dhruv came to me today, very quiet, to ask if he could pay the book fee later. When I asked gently, he explained. At Diwali he received gift money from relatives. On the same day he saw an advertisement for wireless earphones and bought them within the hour. He told me, "I didn't even think. It looked so cool." Now the book fee and three notebooks are due, and he does not want to ask his mother, Nirmala, because she had told him to keep some aside. He looked ashamed. I did not lecture him. I told him mistakes like this are common and that he should speak to his mother today; I will also mention the fee date to her myself.

qa.q: What did Dhruv buy with his Diwali money?
qa.a: Wireless earphones he saw in an advertisement.

qa.q: What was Dhruv feeling when he came to the teacher?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and worried, very quiet, afraid to face his mother after ignoring her advice.

qa.q: What would you advise Dhruv to do now?
qa.a: Talk honestly with his mother today, as the teacher suggested, and next time wait a day before buying something he sees in an advertisement.

qa.q: How might Nirmala feel when she hears about it?
qa.a: She may feel disappointed, but also relieved he told the truth and asked for help.

grounding: A teenager spends festival money on a gadget from an advertisement and then cannot cover the notebook and book fee he needs.

subtype: Approach: buys something on a sudden urge [Pitfall]
passage:
Saturday night

Big mistake today. I had the money from Lohri and Mummy said, "Beta, keep some for your school things." Then this video popped up about a mini speaker with coloured lights and I just ordered it. Didn't even think. Five minutes. It came today and it's fun for about ten minutes. Then Sunaina asked, "Weren't you supposed to buy the new maths guide and notebooks on Monday? And the book fee?" I checked. There's not enough left. My stomach dropped. Now I have to tell Mummy. I feel so stupid. Why didn't I wait even one day? Tomorrow morning I'll tell her before she finds out. Amandeep, next time, sleep on it first.

qa.q: What did Amandeep order after seeing the video?
qa.a: A mini speaker with coloured lights.

qa.q: How does Amandeep feel after Sunaina's question?
qa.a: Amandeep feels sick with worry and foolish; the stomach dropped on realising there wasn't enough left.

qa.q: What could Amandeep do before buying next time?
qa.a: Wait at least a day, as the diary says, and check what school things are needed first.

qa.q: How might Sunaina see the speaker now?
qa.a: Sunaina probably sees it as a fun toy that caused a problem, and may feel a little sorry for pointing it out.

grounding: A teenager buys a gadget on a sudden urge from an advertisement and then cannot afford the notebooks and book fee needed.
